title: streaming-event-anchoring-checksum-framing-and-reconnect-guidance
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Deliver a robust SSE framing and reconnect design that uses cryptographic checksums and lightweight fragment anchoring to: 1) enable safe reassembly on client reconnects, 2) provide compatibility fallbacks for older clients, and 3) preserve function-call/structured-output atomicity. This ticket produces a spec, a set of server-side validators, and an integration test harness for reconnect scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published describing fragment envelope, checksum algorithm choices (CRC32 vs SipHash vs HMAC), and backward-compatibility header negotiation
Server emits fragment envelope with fragment_id, seq_offset, payload_len, anchor_checksum, provenance_path headers for every chunk
Client-facing reconnect protocol documented: resume-window semantics, idempotency token negotiation, and deterministic merge strategy for overlapping fragments
Integration test harness simulates network drop and validates reassembly for 99.9% of synthetic workloads across sequence lengths 8..8192 tokens
Performance analysis shows <3% median tail token-latency change for common batch sizes when checksum envelope is enabled
tasks: Write spec: fragment envelope, header names, and negotiation pairs (server+client) - draft by 2025-01-27
Prototype server-side envelope emission in runtime proxy with CRC32 and optional HMAC - spike by 2025-02-03
Add reassembly library to SDKs: idempotency-key handling, overlap heuristics, and snapshot fallback - implement by 2025-02-14
Create integration test scenarios: 1s-10s outage, packet duplication, out-of-order delivery - run and collect metrics
Evaluate perf and memory impact with real models and report thresholds where envelope can be hardware-accelerated or disabled
notes: We intentionally chose CRC32 for default envelope because it's cheap and implemented in C at runtime; HMAC-SHA256 option is available when clients opt into stronger provenance. Must ensure HMAC keys rotate via KMS and are not used by default for hosted free-tier to avoid key-management burden.
comments: 2025-01-22 - Ava Martinez: Initial spec draft done. Added illustrative diagrams for fragment envelopes. Posting to #streaming-arch for early feedback.

2025-01-24 - Priya Raman (review): Strong preference for HMAC when customer_impact==high; suggest negotiation header X-RI-Fragment-Auth: none|crc32|hmac-sha256. Also flagged telemetry points for reconnect frequency and partial-reassembly rate.

2025-01-30 - Liam O'Connell: Spike completed. Server can attach envelope with ~1% CPU overhead when using CRC32. HMAC spike shows 6-8% cost on p4d benchmarks. Adding opt-in config per deployment tier.

2025-02-04 - Security (K. Huang): KMS integration required for HMAC keys; sync with infra team. Also raised concern about leaking payload lengths - switched to optional obfuscation flag 'payload_len_masked' in envelope to mitigate fingerprinting.

2025-02-07 - PM Emily Chen: For Dedicated customers we should enable HMAC by default behind a feature flag and include an SLA note about resume guarantees. Marked as release candidate for runtime-1.25 if integration tests pass.

2025-02-09 - Design (Marco Silva): UX note - Console should surface a 'Resume success rate' metric and provide an example timeline showing fragment reassembly across reconnects. Will add dashboard mockups to the Confluence page.
progress_update: 2025-02-10 - Server-side CRC32 envelope merged to runtime branch. SDK reassembly lib PR is in review with unit tests for overlap heuristics. Integration harness shows successful reassembly in 98.6% of runs for worst-case packet reordering; investigating edge-case gaps around large multi-fragment tool-call boundaries.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: HMAC increases CPU cost and key management complexity. Mitigation: default to CRC32; make HMAC opt-in per deployment tier. Risk: older clients that expect raw JSONL may misinterpret envelope headers. Mitigation: compatibility negotiation header and a 'legacy-mode' transport shim that strips envelopes for approved clients.
implementation_notes: Envelope schema: X-RI-Fragment-Id, X-RI-Seq-Offset, X-RI-Payload-Len (optional masked), X-RI-Anchor-CRC32, X-RI-Auth-Type, X-RI-Provenance. Fragments MUST be treated as append-only; server retains last N fragment anchors in a short-lived cache (configurable TTL) to assist reconcilers. On reconnect client presents Last-Received-Fragment-Id and optionally Last-Verified-Checksum to request delta streams.
qa_plan: Fuzz reconnects with variable MTU, simulate partial writes and duplication. Measure reassembly correctness, duplicate suppression, and function-call boundary preservation. Add flaky test annotations for networked CI. Validate compatibility shim against old SDK v0.8.1.
owner_notes: Next steps: schedule cross-team sync with SDK, Security, and Console owners. Add a small migration note for customers using custom proxies (NGINX/Envoy) describing needed header passthrough rules.
